Moving Average Help: Moving Average calculates the average value over a sliding window of data points. For each point, it looks at neighboring points within the window size and computes their mean. This reduces noise and reveals trends in the data.
Loess Smoothing Help: Loess (Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing) fits multiple local regression models to subsets of the data. It creates a smooth curve that follows the data patterns more closely than a moving average, especially for non-linear trends.

about_benjamin: Benjamin Azoulay is a senior civil servant and maritime affairs administrator. He is currently seconded as a senior data scientist at the Ministry of Finance.
about_project_p1: Gallicagram is a lockdown project that got out of hand. In 2021, Benjamin showed Benoît, a vague acquaintance, a snippet of code he wrote to plot (ugly) frequency curves of phrases in the French National Library's corpora. Benoît, whose coding skills were barely any better back then, exclaimed that it would be a brilliant idea to wrap this code in a Shiny app so that a computer-illiterate historian could plot curves too. Fast forward 5 years and a few thousand hours of work later, Benjamin and Benoît are now friends and slightly less incompetent. The project has expanded significantly, comprising several facets:

tv_corpus_gaps_note: This corpus is built by continuously recording rolling-news channels. The recording is occasionally interrupted, so some days are missing from the corpus. They do not show up as a drop but as a break in the line: where there is no line, there is no data.
tv_corpus_asr_note: The transcripts are produced automatically by speech recognition (Whisper). Everyday vocabulary is recognised well, proper nouns less so, especially recent ones: a name that has only just entered the news may be misspelt or replaced by a more common word, and is therefore undercounted. Curves for recent proper nouns should be read with caution.
cairn_context_link_note: Cairn does not allow occurrences to be read from within Gallicagram, so the search opens on their site instead, with the word and the selected journals. Cairn can only filter by relative period (current year, last 3, 5 or 10 years), so the results are not restricted to the year you clicked.
press_search_warning: These articles come from the search engine of {{name}}, restricted to the period you clicked. They are a sample of what the newspaper published, not the occurrences counted in the curve.
press_loose_matching_note: This engine also returns near matches (“retraites” can bring up “retrait”).
press_up_to_end_note: Its results come newest first, so for a long period only its last days appear.
press_no_results: The newspaper's search engine found nothing for this period. Google may do better: see the link above.
press_link_note: The search engine of {{site}} cannot be restricted to a date from Gallicagram, so the search opens on Google instead, limited to {{site}} and to the period you clicked. Google's date filter is approximate.
press_own_search_note: The search engine of {{site}} only answers your browser, not Gallicagram, so it opens in a new tab, limited to the period you clicked.
press_failed_note: The search on {{name}} could not be loaded. It can be run on Google instead, limited to {{site}} and to the period you clicked.
presse_moderne_help: This corpus adds up every modern press outlet (except Le Marin, a trade paper). For each date, the occurrences in all outlets are summed, then divided by the total word count of all outlets: each outlet weighs according to how much it publishes, so dailies weigh more than weeklies. Not every outlet covers the whole period, so the make-up of the corpus changes over time.
wildcard_help: Use * to add up, in one line, every word that starts this way (? stands for a single letter)
any_word_help: Use _ for any word: every phrase with a word in that place is added up in one line
joker_syntax_help: Put _ where you are looking for a word: “guerre _ allemagne” gives the most frequent words between “guerre” and “allemagne”. Without _, the joker goes after the words typed, as many times as Length asks. On the Gallica press, the search cannot start with _.
score_llr_help: The most significantly associated words, given how frequent they are on their own (Dunning's test). Favours frequent, solid associations.
score_pmi_help: How many times more often than chance the word appears there. Favours rare, exclusive associations: pair it with a high minimum count.
score_logdice_help: Association score (at most 14) that does not depend on corpus size: comparable across periods and corpora.
min_count_help: Words seen less often are left out: association scores are unstable on rare words.
joker_underscore_help: Put _ where you are looking for a word: the most frequent words in that place are listed. Without _, one is added after the words typed. On the Gallica press, the search cannot start with _.
joker_wildcard_help: A word that starts this way: each form is listed separately
nearby_syntax_help: Type one or two exact words (no * or _): the most frequent words nearby are listed, within a window set by Length. On the Gallica press, only the words that follow are counted.
